cards.note:
The section of the A1 within the Central District (Dibete to Tonota) has a parallel paved road the entire way, which is not in use or painted with road lines. Parallel roads are basically only found on the A1, and this section is distinguishable from the A1 north of Francistown because it is not newly paved/painted.

The map does not show the parallel road in the south of this section, so remember it stretches across the entire Central District if you are trying to pinpoint.

The section of the A1 north of Francistown has a road that runs parallel the whole way to the border to its east. It is often a light gray colour. This section of the A1 looks recently paved compared to other parts of the A1 which also have a parallel road.

West A2 = Most identifiable road in Botswana (the only paved road with overcast coverage)

No electricity poles means you are between the Chobokwane junction and the A2/A3 junction. This coverage also has the sun trying to shine through the clouds instead of complete overcast coverage, but it is still a lot cloudier than almost all Botswana coverage.

West A2 = Most identifiable road in Botswana (the only paved road with overcast coverage)

One electricity pole means you are between Tshootsha and Chobokwane. The pole should be a shorter pole that stays close and to the north of the road. Make sure a second taller pole is not also visible, even if in the far distance or to the south, as that puts you in the red section instead.

West A2 = Most identifiable road in Botswana (the only paved road with overcast coverage)

Two electricity poles means you are between Charleshill and Tshootsha. The first pole should be a shorter one thats stays close and to the north of the road. The second pole is a taller one and can be in any direction and distance relative to you, north or south. However, it will always be visible, just make sure you check thoroughly if you can't initially see it. Finally, use the road angle to know if you are east or west of Karakubis.

This eastern part of the A3 is identifiable by the colourful trees on the sides of the road. To tell this apart from other similar coverage, look at the road. This area is not recently paved, and the grass is basically touching the yellow road lines.

The A32 is an identifiable road located west of the main salt pans in central Botswana. The most noticeable thing is the red/grey tint to the dead-looking trees either side of the road. Combine this with the white dirt on the sides of the road to know you are here.

The highlighted locations are basically the only sections of road in the entire country where large fields of small crop plants are visible in rows like these. Use the road angle to know which of the two sections you are in.

A significant portion of the A33 is made up of a newly paved road. This road is very wide, has no roadlines yet, and both sides of the road have almost been completely dug up. No other section of road in Botswana looks quite like this.

A significant portion of the A33 has a road under construction next to it. This road can have dug up orange soil, white soil, be somewhat paved, or just have the long grass cut. Regardless, when combined with the relatively green trees, you will almost certainly be on this section of road.

This section of the A33 is distinguishable by combining the good-quality road with either the colourful trees or the tall golden grass that has a shine to it from distance.

Nearby areas can have similar coverage, but this road looks recently paved/painted and no other road with similar coverage is as vertical on the map as this section is. You will also see an electricity pole on this section of road between Nata and Maposa.

The road quality of the A35 is relatively bad with the side paving being uneven, and the faded yellow line is usually on this part of the road. There is also a lot of yellow grass, with yellow and green shrubs and trees.

Only a small section in the centre of the A35 has an electricity pole both east and west (excluding in villages, which looks different). Additionally, an even smaller section has the west electricity lines seemingly broken, and the lines can either be seen running in trees or on the ground.

The road quality of the A35 is relatively bad with the side paving being uneven, and the faded yellow line is usually on this part of the road. There is also a lot of yellow grass, with yellow and green shrubs and trees.

You will only find an electricity pole to the east of the road below Tsau, which makes for an amazing region guess.

The road quality of the A35 is relatively bad with the side paving being uneven, and the faded yellow line is usually on this part of the road. There is also a lot of yellow grass, with yellow and green shrubs and trees.

Small villages run up the entire A35. If you see electricity poles which go across the road, where there are multiple lines on one side of the road, or rare coverage where none are visible, you will be in/near a village.

The road quality of the A35 is relatively bad with the side paving being uneven, and the faded yellow line is usually on this part of the road. There is also a lot of yellow grass, with yellow and green shrubs and trees.

Unfortunately a majority of the A35 has an electricity pole to the west of the road. It does at least put you north of Tsau and rule out a small section in the middle.

All helpful numbers in Botswana will be 7 digits long, not 8.

If you find a 7 digit number that is 24X XXXX, it is based in Francistown.

All helpful numbers in Botswana will be 7 digits long, not 8.

If you find a 7 digit number that is 3XX XXXX, it is based in Gaborone. However, many companies that provide services outside Gaborone are still based in the capital which can make this area code a little less reliable. Try to find a number on a building rather than a vehicle or advertising sign if possible.

All helpful numbers in Botswana will be 7 digits long, not 8.

If you find a 7 digit number that is 68X XXXX, it is based in Maun.

The Chobe River, which makes up part of Botswana's northern border, is rarely seen but easy to recognize. It can have patches of tall grass peeking out the top of the water and a variety of wildlife can often be seen in the area, including elephants, warthogs, and much more. If you can see the wide river, you will almost certainly be on one of the paths in a circled zone.

One of the most recognizable unpaved roads in Botswana is north of Maun. Starting in Shorobe, this road has white sand and bright green trees the entire way. Try to use the road angle and road width to your advantage too, for example the central coverage has a lot of curves in the road and goes north-west.

The town of Shoshong and the surrounding roads are identifiable. There is a long stretch of tall hills to the north and south and it generally looks like the hills completely surround the area. The few other places in Botswana where hills surround the area have much closer hills, but the ones around Shoshong are visible even from far away.

cards.a: South West - Border with South Africa
cards.note:
The furthest south-west road in Botswana runs along the border with South Africa. You can tell you are here by the redness of the road and surrounding sand/dirt and the pale-green grass which is visible a lot of the time. Additionally, there is almost always a slight hill to the north (sometimes south too).

One important thing to note is the car drives the road from east to west (of course accounting for the road's bends). This can help rule out certain spots of road that wouldn't make logical sense if you want to try and 5k.

Tsodilo Hills is a world heritage site in north-west Botswana branching off the A35. The single dirt road that runs from the A35 to Tsodilo Hills can be recognized by combining the white sand and the lush vegetation with the road/driving direction (west south-west). It looks a lot like the road north of Maun but that road never goes this direction.

Additionally, the Tsodilo Hills can be seen in most locations in the half of the road closer to the Hills than the A35, since the hills themselves are very tall for Botswana standards.

The road furthest west in Botswana is easy to identify. It looks the same as most of the other unpaved roads found in the west of the country, but this road is identifiable from the electricity pole to the east of the road. This does not diverge from the road once.

All the highlighted roads look similar with white sand for the road and surrounded by either orange sand or yellow grass. They are also unpaved and have no electricity poles. If you think you are here, try to remember the google car directions to know where would be best to guess.
